questions.def: 'Had something done' uses the past participle.
questions.question: I had my car ___ yesterday.

questions.def: 'Got something done' uses the past participle.
questions.question: She got her hair ___ at the salon.

questions.def: Future causative structure: will have something done.
questions.question: I will ___ my windows tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Made' requires the base form of the verb.
questions.question: He made me ___ the report again.

questions.def: 'Let' requires the base form of the verb.
questions.question: The manager let him ___ early today.

questions.def: Past causative: had something done by someone.
questions.question: She ___ her computer by a technician.

questions.def: 'Get something done' always uses the past participle.
questions.question: I must get my watch ___.

questions.def: 'Had something done' needs the past participle.
questions.question: The company had the documents ___ immediately.

questions.def: Future intention, causative: have something done.
questions.question: I'm going to ___ my hair this afternoon.

questions.def: When 'have' means 'cause', use base form after person.
questions.question: The teacher had the students ___ an essay.

questions.def: 'Got something done' uses past participle.
questions.question: They got the package ___ to their home.

questions.def: Present perfect causative: have something done.
questions.question: I ___ my email every morning.

questions.def: 'Is having' needs the past participle: designed.
questions.question: The company is having a new website ___.

questions.def: 'Let' requires the base form of the verb.
questions.question: He let his dog ___ outside.

questions.def: Future causative structure: will have something done.
questions.question: We will ___ our groceries this week.

questions.def: 'Had something done' requires the past participle.
questions.question: They had their house ___ after the storm.

questions.def: 'Got something done' uses past participle.
questions.question: She got her thesis ___ by a professor.

questions.def: Past causative: had something done.
questions.question: I ___ the documents yesterday.

questions.def: 'Get something done' needs past participle.
questions.question: I will get the report ___ by tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Let' requires the base form of the verb.
questions.question: The director let the actors ___ their lines.

questions.def: Past causative: had something done.
questions.question: She ___ her passport before the trip.

questions.def: 'Are going to have' needs past participle.
questions.question: They are going to have their house ___.

questions.def: 'Got something done' requires past participle.
questions.question: He got the message ___ immediately.

questions.def: The structure 'have something done' implies someone else did it.
questions.question: I had my car ___ yesterday. It looks great now.

questions.def: 'Get someone to do' needs 'to' before the infinitive verb.
questions.question: She got her brother ___ her with the heavy boxes.

questions.def: We are arranging for someone else to repair our house.
questions.question: We are ___ our house next month.

questions.def: 'Let someone do' doesn't need 'to' before the infinitive.
questions.question: They let us ___ the office late.

questions.def: 'Have something done' uses the past participle.
questions.question: I'll have the report ___ by Friday.

questions.def: Implies someone else will cut your hair for you.
questions.question: I need to ___ my hair. It's too long.

questions.def: 'Make someone do' requires the base form of the verb.
questions.question: The teacher made the students ___ the exercise again.
